projects.title: Succession Law Reform in Post-Socialist European States: Comparative Foundations and Policy Options
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project conducted a comparative legal analysis of succession law reform trajectories in six post-socialist European states (Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Bulgaria), focusing on the tension between testamentary freedom and protected heirship. Research activities included legislative text analysis, a systematic review of published court decisions across the six jurisdictions (approximately 900 decisions coded), 47 semi-structured interviews with notaries and judges in Serbia, and two comparative workshops held in Novi Sad (2022) and Ljubljana (2023). The project produced draft legislative recommendations for reform of the Serbian succession law provisions within the Civil Code drafting process and delivered a publicly accessible bilingual (Serbian/English) database of post-1990 succession legislation in the six target states. Three journal articles and one edited book chapter were submitted from the project.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Ljubljana
Institute of Private International Law and Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Succession in the Western Balkans–EU Border Region: Legal Uncertainty and Practical Solutions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the practical difficulties encountered by families in the Hungary–Serbia border region when dealing with cross-border estates after the entry into force of EU Succession Regulation 650/2012. The Faculty of Law, Novi Sad, led the work package on legal analysis and practitioner training. Activities included mapping of conflict-of-law problems through 60 notary case file reviews in Subotica and Sombor, preparation of a bilingual practitioner guide (Hungarian/Serbian) on cross-border estate procedures, and delivery of five joint training seminars for notaries and court officials on both sides of the border. The project also produced a policy brief addressed to the Serbian Ministry of Justice recommending bilateral treaty negotiations with Hungary and Croatia. The Novi Sad team consisted of three researchers and one doctoral student.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Pécs
Notarial Chamber of Vojvodina
Hungarian Chamber of Notaries, Southern Region

projects.title: Urban Property Governance: Legal Frameworks for Sustainable Residential Building Management in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines the legal conditions for effective governance of multi-unit residential buildings across six Western Balkan jurisdictions, comparing property rights frameworks, homeowners association rules, and public enforcement mechanisms. The research team collects court decisions, administrative records, and building management data from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. One work package, to which Mladenović contributes, is dedicated to the property law treatment of shared technical infrastructure—heating systems, elevators, and utility risers—and how maintenance costs are allocated when infrastructure serves mixed residential and commercial units. Outputs include comparative country reports, a model legislative commentary, and a policy brief directed at the relevant Serbian ministry.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Administrative Justice Traditions and EU Integration in the Western Balkans: Historical Roots, Present Deficits, Reform Paths
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the relationship between inherited administrative-judicial institutions and the effectiveness of EU-driven administrative justice reforms across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. The research team combined archival and doctrinal legal history with empirical analysis of court statistics and a structured interview programme (n=48 interviews with judges, lawyers, and civil servants). The project produced seven journal articles, two edited book chapters, a policy brief submitted to the Serbian Ministry of Justice, and a comparative database of administrative court legislation in the region covering 1919 to 2023, made publicly available through the Faculty of Law repository.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo
Iustinianus Primus Faculty of Law, Saints Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Faculty of Law, University of Montenegro, Podgorica

projects.title: Decision Support Frameworks for Strategic Investment Planning in South-East European Public Institutions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated multi-criteria decision support frameworks specifically adapted to institutional, regulatory, and data-availability constraints of public organisations in South-East Europe. Activities included a cross-country survey of decision practices in 45 public institutions across Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro; development of tailored AHP and fuzzy TOPSIS instruments; and delivery of three stakeholder workshops. The project produced a methodological guide for procurement committees and budget officers, piloted in four Serbian municipalities. Two journal articles and one conference paper were published. The project was hosted at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, with research collaboration from partner universities in Niš and Skopje.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje, North Macedonia

projects.title: Финансијска дигитализација и понашање старијих корисника у Србији: панел студија
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат финансира трећу и четврту таласну фазу longitudinalne панел студије започете 2015. године, проширујући узорак испитаника из Војводине на Централну Србију. Поред анкетних метода, уводи се анализа анонимизованих трансакционих података у сарадњи с партнерском штедионицом. Истражују се ефекти политике обавезне дигитализације исплате пензија на понашање корисника и субјективно финансијско благостање. Планирани излазни резултати укључују три научна рада у рецензираним часописима, скуп анонимизованих панел података доступан за поновну употребу и извештај за доносиоце политика на српском језику.
partners: Економски факултет, Универзитет у Београду
Регионална штедионица Панонија (измишљена организација)

projects.title: Semantic Standards for Interoperable Public Procurement in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a family of OWL 2 ontology profiles and SHACL validation constraint sets covering the procurement systems of Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Montenegro, and North Macedonia. Core outputs include a regional procurement ontology registry, a set of SPARQL-based alignment tests, and a bilingual (Serbian/English) ontology documentation portal. The project also produced policy briefs submitted to the national public procurement offices of all four countries and to the Regional Cooperation Council in Sarajevo. Two PhD students completed dissertations within the project.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Sarajevo
Faculty of Economics, University of Montenegro
Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University Skopje

projects.title: Cross-Border Public Procurement Interoperability Along the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSBUY addressed the practical barriers preventing joint cross-border procurement under the Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme. Krstić led the semantic interoperability work package, which delivered a semantic mediation layer connecting the Hungarian EKR and Serbian e-procurement platforms, a shared SKOS qualification vocabulary in Hungarian and Serbian, and a set of RDF mapping rules for bidder registration data exchange. The project involved piloting joint simplified tenders with two contracting authorities (one municipality on each side of the border) and produced a replication guide for other border region programmes.
partners: Pécs Regional Development Agency
Public Procurement Office of Serbia (Belgrade)
City of Subotica – Department of Urban Planning and Finance
University of Pécs, Department of Information Systems

projects.title: Fiscal Credibility, Debt Market Development, and European Integration Trajectories in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled a harmonised quarterly dataset on sovereign borrowing costs, fiscal frameworks, and exchange rate arrangements for six Western Balkan economies covering 1998–2023. It tested competing hypotheses about the drivers of fiscal credibility signals visible in secondary bond market spreads, with particular attention to the interaction between IMF programme anchors, domestic fiscal rules, and currency regime choices. The team produced seven working papers, three journal submissions, and a policy brief series distributed to the Serbian Ministry of Finance and the EU Delegation in Belgrade. A public dataset of cleaned and documented spread series is being prepared for release via the University of Novi Sad data repository.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Montenegro, Podgorica
Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
School of Economics and Business, University of Sarajevo

projects.title: Corporate Tax Base Erosion Through Transfer Pricing in Central and Eastern Europe: Measurement, Determinants, and Policy Responses
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project constructs a longitudinal database linking Serbian Business Registers Agency financial statements, customs declaration microdata, and Orbis records for approximately 1,200 foreign-owned subsidiaries active in Serbia between 2010 and 2022. The database is used to estimate annual corporate income tax revenue losses attributable to transfer pricing manipulation, to identify the industry sectors and ownership structures where manipulation is most intense, and to evaluate the effectiveness of Serbian legislative responses to OECD BEPS recommendations. The project also includes a comparative module covering Hungary, Romania, and Croatia. A policy brief series targets the Serbian Tax Administration, the Ministry of Finance, and the Secretariat for Finance of the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
University of Belgrade, Faculty of Economics
Institute of Economic Sciences, Belgrade

projects.title: Islamic Finance Regulatory Frameworks for the Western Balkans: Comparative Analysis and Legislative Recommendations
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project produced a systematic comparative analysis of legal and regulatory preconditions for introducing Islamic finance products in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The team reviewed banking, tax, securities, and insolvency legislation in each jurisdiction, conducted interviews with central bank officials and commercial bankers, and ran two stakeholder workshops with representatives of Muslim community organisations and finance practitioners. The primary output is a set of three jurisdiction-specific legislative reform proposals, each accompanied by a regulatory impact assessment. Secondary outputs include a regional database of Islamic finance legal provisions and a university-level teaching case collection. Total budget approximately RSD 12 million.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Sarajevo
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Green Sukuk Market Development and EU Sustainable Finance Integration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project examines the conditions under which green sukuk could be issued by public or private issuers in Hungary and Serbia as a tool for financing environmental infrastructure. Orlović leads the work package on regulatory harmonisation, examining alignment between green sukuk frameworks and the EU Taxonomy Regulation and the European Green Bond Standard. Partner activities cover market demand analysis and investor profiling in both countries. The project includes a joint training programme for financial sector professionals in both jurisdictions delivered through a series of five workshops, and a policy brief addressed to the Hungarian and Serbian ministries of finance.
partners: Department of Finance, Corvinus University of Budapest
Green Investment Advisory Centre Novi Sad (GIAC NS)
Hungarian Development Bank Research Institute

projects.title: Financial Reporting Quality and Capital Market Development in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project builds a harmonised, longitudinal database of financial statements and earnings management indicators for all non-financial firms listed on the stock exchanges of Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2010 to 2022. Key activities include collection and standardisation of raw financial statement data, estimation of accrual-based and real-activities earnings management proxies using multiple benchmark models, and analysis of the relationship between reporting quality and capital market outcomes including liquidity, cost of capital, and institutional investor participation. The project also compares regulatory and enforcement frameworks across the three jurisdictions to identify governance factors associated with higher reporting quality, and produces policy briefs addressed to the relevant securities commissions.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of East Sarajevo
Institute of Economic Sciences, Belgrade

projects.title: Knowledge Management Frameworks for Regional Administration: Comparative Capacity Assessment in Serbia, Romania and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je obuhvatao komparativnu procenu zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u 36 regionalnih i lokalnih javnih institucija u Srbiji, Rumuniji i Mađarskoj. Istraživački tim razvio je zajednički dijagnostički protokol koji je primenjen u sva tri nacionalna konteksta, a nalazi su korišćeni za dizajn programa izgradnje kapaciteta namenjenih rukovodiocima u javnom sektoru. Kovačević je bila lider radnog paketa zaduženog za razvoj metodologije i koordinaciju istraživačkih aktivnosti u Srbiji. Projekat je rezultovao zajedničkim priručnikom za samodijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem i nizom radionica za javne službenike u pograničnim regionima.
partners: Universitatea de Vest din Timișoara, Facultatea de Științe Economice
Pécsi Tudományegyetem, Közgazdaságtudományi Kar
Regionalna razvojna agencija Banat, Zrenjanin
Asociația pentru Dezvoltare Regională Vest, Timișoara

projects.title: Merenje i unapređenje kapaciteta upravljanja znanjem u organima javne uprave u Vojvodini
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je finansiran od strane Pokrajinskog sekretarijata za visoko obrazovanje i naučnoistraživačku delatnost i usmeren je na razvoj i validaciju alatki za samodijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem prilagođenih specifičnostima pokrajinske i lokalne uprave u Vojvodini. U okviru projekta sproveden je anketni upitnik u 22 opštinske uprave i pet pokrajinskih organa (N = 340), a rezultati su korišćeni za izradu javno dostupnog izveštaja o stanju upravljanja znanjem u Vojvodini. Projekat je takođe podržao izradu doktorske disertacije jednog od članova istraživačkog tima.
partners: Tehnički fakultet „Mihajlo Pupin“, Zrenjanin, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Pokrajinski sekretarijat za regionalnu politiku, međuregionalnu saradnju i lokalnu samoupravu
Stalna konferencija gradova i opština Srbije – Regionalna kancelarija Novi Sad

projects.title: Lean Production Readiness and Performance in the Serbian Food Processing Sector: Diagnostic Tools and Implementation Support
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate diagnostic and implementation support tools for lean adoption in Serbian food processing companies. Activities included large-scale survey data collection from over 100 firms, longitudinal follow-up of kaizen events in selected companies, and the development of a web-based readiness self-assessment instrument piloted with twelve companies. The project produced five peer-reviewed publications, one edited book chapter, and a practitioner guide distributed through the Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina. A database of baseline operational metrics from participating firms was compiled and is maintained at the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin'. The project funded one doctoral student whose dissertation focused on performance measurement in lean food companies.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Prioritization Maturity and Technology Transfer in Serbian Manufacturing Firms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje u kojoj meri zrelost procesa prioritizacije R&D portfolija utiče na uspešnost transfera tehnologije u prerađivačkim preduzećima Srbije. Istraživanje obuhvata longitudinalnu studiju na uzorku od 40 preduzeća praćenih tokom tri godine, uz godišnje merenje RPM-MM skor vrednosti i indikatora transfera (broj licenci, spin-off preduzeća, zajedničkih patenata s istraživačkim institucijama). Projektom je predviđena i izrada javno dostupnog priručnika za primenu alata prioritizacije, namenjen preduzećima bez OR stručnjaka, kao i organizovanje godišnje konferencije za praktičare u Zrenjaninu.
partners: Tehnički fakultet „Mihajlo Pupin“, Zrenjanin
Institut Mihajlo Pupin, Beograd
Privredna komora Vojvodine

projects.title: Cross-border Agricultural Monitoring and Yield Forecasting Using Copernicus Data in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish a shared satellite-based monitoring service for agricultural parcels in the cross-border region spanning South Bačka (Serbia) and Csongrád-Csanád (Hungary). The BioSense Institute was responsible for processing Sentinel-2 time series, constructing parcel databases from national LPIS sources, and delivering seasonal yield forecast maps. Branislav Lekić contributed the yield modelling component, adapting and validating regression models trained on Serbian data for application to Hungarian parcels. The project produced a web-based dashboard for regional agricultural authorities and published protocols for harmonising cross-border parcel datasets. Final yield forecast maps for winter wheat and maize were delivered to partner organisations at the end of each growing season.
partners: Department of Geoinformatics, University of Pécs
South Bačka Regional Development Agency, Novi Sad
Csongrád-Csanád County Government, Hungary

projects.title: Operational Crop Yield Estimation for the Vojvodina Region Using Fused Optical and SAR Satellite Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CROPSENSE addressed the practical deployment of parcel-level yield prediction for five major crops grown in Vojvodina, with particular focus on reducing dependence on cloud-free optical imagery by incorporating Sentinel-1 SAR data. Branislav Lekić led the work package on data fusion and model development, overseeing the assembly of a multi-year parcel dataset from combine-harvester records provided by three agricultural cooperatives, satellite data processing, and the design of a modular prediction pipeline. The project produced open-source Python tooling for time series fusion, a calibrated yield model ensemble, and a set of validation reports for each crop type. Dissemination included two journal articles, one conference paper, and a technical report delivered to the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agricultural Cooperative Zlatna Njiva, Sombor
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
